All paths relative to /mnt/data1/gsn27/here/CMSSW_16_1_0_pre2/src/RecoTracker/LSTCore/ unless absolute.

=====================================================================
1. COMBINATORIC LOOP STRUCTURE
=====================================================================

Kernel launch sequence (src/alpaka/LSTEvent.dev.cc, LSTEvent::createTriplets(), lines 393-529):
1. CountSegmentConnections[ReduceMem] (Triplet.h:721) — precompute exact/upper-bound per-segment T3 counts. Workdiv {nLowerModules,1,1} blocks x {1,16,16} threads (LSTEvent.dev.cc:395). Kernel selected by `reduceMemByFullPrecompute_` flag (LSTEvent.dev.cc:408-411).
2. CreateTripletArrayRanges (Triplet.h:803) — single-block 1024-thread prefix-sum kernel; per-module occupancy = sum of `segments.connectedMax()` over the module's inner segments (Triplet.h:826-834); writes `ranges.tripletModuleOccupancy()`, `ranges.tripletModuleIndices()`, `ranges.nTotalTrips()`.
3. Host readback of `nTotalTrips` -> allocate TripletsSoA with exactly nTotalTriplets rows (LSTEvent.dev.cc:425-431). memset nTriplets/totOccupancy/partOf*/connectedMax/connectedLSMax to 0 (LSTEvent.dev.cc:439-455).
4. Host builds `index_gpu` list of "nonZero" modules: modules with nConnectedModules != 0 AND nSegments != 0 (LSTEvent.dev.cc:484-492).
5. CreateTriplets[ReduceMem] (Triplet.h:519), workdiv {nonZeroModules,1,1} blocks x {1,16,16} threads (LSTEvent.dev.cc:500).
6. AddTripletRangesToEventExplicit (Triplet.h:844) — fills ranges.tripletRanges()[i] = [start, start+n-1] or [-1,-1] (Triplet.h:852-860).

Loop structure of CreateTripletsT (Triplet.h:610-713):
- Grid-z loop over nonZero inner ("innerInner") lower modules: `uniform_groups_z(acc, nonZeroModules)` (Triplet.h:610); module index from `index_gpu` (Triplet.h:615). Skips if nConnectedModules==0 (Triplet.h:619-621) or nInnerSegments==0 (Triplet.h:623-626).
- Block-y loop over inner segments of that module: `uniform_elements_y(acc, nInnerSegments)`, innerSegmentIndex = segmentRanges[module][0] + idx (Triplet.h:631-633).
- Middle module = `segments.outerLowerModuleIndices()[innerSegmentIndex]` (Triplet.h:635). NOTE: no direct module-map lookup in T3 building — the module connection map (modules.moduleMap/nConnectedModules) was already applied at LS building, so T3 pairing is purely "LS chaining": inner LS(modA->modB) x all LS starting on modB. The only module-map touch is the nConnectedModules != 0 skip (Triplet.h:619; host prefilter LSTEvent.dev.cc:487).
- Per inner segment, hoist T3InnerSegData once (Triplet.h:638-639, struct at 19-34, loader at 45-77): x1,y1,x2,y2, rt1,rt2, drt, rt_InSeg (1 sqrt), sdIn_alpha=dPhiChange (__H2F), sin/cos(sdIn_alpha) (+4 more sin/cos if EEE endcap path), subdets.
- Block-x loop over outer segments of the middle module: `uniform_elements_x(acc, nOuterSegments)` (Triplet.h:642-643). So the candidate set is (inner LS) x (all LS of middle module) — MD sharing is enforced by a cut, not by indexing.
- Selection chain per candidate (see section 2). Two execution modes:
  * ReduceMem=true (CreateTripletsReduceMem, Triplet.h:658-665,718): single pass — MD-match + pointing constraint inline, then tryAddTriplet runs the full algo (RZ + DNN) immediately.
  * ReduceMem=false (default CreateTriplets, Triplet.h:667-712): two-phase per module. Step 1: pairs passing MD-match + pointing constraint are counted with a block-shared `matchCount` atomic (Triplet.h:668) and their (innerSeg,outerSeg) written to `triplets.preAllocatedSegmentIndices()` at tripletModuleIndices[module]+mIdx (Triplet.h:685-686). syncBlockThreads (Triplet.h:693). Step 2: flat-threaded loop `for (i = flatThreadIdxXY; i < matchCount; i += blockSize)` re-reads the stored pairs and runs tryAddTriplet (RZ+DNN) (Triplet.h:699-712). This load-balances the expensive part across the whole 16x16 block.

Occupancy caps: there are NO hardcoded per-module cap constants for T3s anymore. The cap is the DYNAMIC per-module value `ranges.tripletModuleOccupancy()[module]` computed by the precount (CountSegmentConnections -> CreateTripletArrayRanges). Enforcement in tryAddTriplet: atomicAdd totOccupancyTriplets; if >= tripletModuleOccupancy -> drop with WARNINGS printf (Triplet.h:575-587); else atomicAdd nTriplets and write at tripletModuleIndices[module]+idx (Triplet.h:588-590).
- Non-ReduceMem: precount counts pairs passing only MD-match + pointing constraint (Triplet.h:756-793 with ReduceMem=false, `counts=true` unconditionally at 768) — an upper bound on real T3s, so the cap can never truncate real triplets (RZ+DNN only shrink the set).
- ReduceMem: precount runs the FULL chain including RZ and DNN (Triplet.h:769-790), so allocation is exact but the whole selection is computed twice per event.
Triplet index is unique per module; `preAllocatedSegmentIndices` reuses the same rows later overwritten by `segmentIndices` etc. of accepted T3s.

CountSegmentConnectionsT loop structure (Triplet.h:721-798) mirrors CreateTriplets: grid-z over ALL nLowerModules (not the index_gpu list), y over inner segments, x over outer segments of middle module; MD-shared check at 756, pointing constraint at 765, then atomicAdd segments.connectedMax()[innerSegmentIndex] (Triplet.h:792).

=====================================================================
2. SELECTION CHAIN, IN ORDER
=====================================================================

(S1) MD-sharing (topological). Triplet.h:645-647: `segments.mdIndices()[innerSeg][1] != segments.mdIndices()[outerSeg][0] -> reject`. Physics: the two LSs must share the middle MiniDoublet (T3 = 3 MDs). No IP assumption. This is the dominant reject (most outer segments of the middle module start on a different MD).

(S2) Pointing constraint / betaIn cut. passPointingConstraint, Triplet.h:390-437, called at Triplet.h:655 (and 765 in the counting kernel).
- Physics: betaIn = sdIn_alpha - [phi(hit3-hit1) - anchorPhi(hit1)] is the angle between the inner-segment direction (via its dPhiChange) and the chord from hit1 to hit3; for a real track of pT >= ptCut this angle is bounded by the sagitta. Implemented algebraically without atan2: sinBetaIn = sin(a)*dot - cos(a)*cross with cross = x1*y3-y1*x3, dot = x3*x1+y3*y1-rt1^2 (Triplet.h:402-416,434-436); cut is sinBetaIn^2 < sin(betaInCut)^2 * (cross^2+dot^2) plus cos(betaIn)>0 sign check.
- Threshold: betaInCut = asin(min((drt_tl_axis - rt_InSeg) * k2Rinv1GeVf / ptCut, kSinAlphaMax)) + 0.02f/drt_InSeg (Triplet.h:397-400). k2Rinv1GeVf = (2.99792458e-3*3.8)/2 (interface/alpaka/Common.h:35), kSinAlphaMax = 0.95 (Common.h:37), ptCut default 0.8 GeV, 0.02/drt slop term.
- IP assumption: YES, twofold. (a) sdIn_alpha = segment dPhiChange is defined relative to the beamline: dPhiChange = phi(displacement) - anchorPhi(innerMD) (Segment.h:371-372), where anchorPhi is the azimuth of the position vector FROM THE ORIGIN. (b) the dot/cross terms use the hit-1 position vector r1 from the origin (Triplet.h:412-413). A displaced track violates the underlying "segment points back to beamline" relation. No kDeltaZLum term appears in Triplet.h (kDeltaZLum = 15 cm, Common.h:38, is used only in MD/LS/pixel code).
- EEE special case (inner+middle+outer all Endcap): test both dPhiChangeMin and dPhiChangeMax variants and take the one with smaller |betaIn| (Triplet.h:418-432).

(S3) Circle fit degeneracy (implicit). computeRadiusFromThreeAnchorHits (interface/Circle.h:11-42), called at Triplet.h:475-476: exact circle through the 3 anchor hits; collinear or r^2<0 -> radius = -1 (Circle.h:31-36). Not a direct reject, but radius<0 forces the RZ linear fallback branch (Triplet.h:311).

(S4) RZ constraint (r-z helix-consistency chi2). passRZConstraint, Triplet.h:134-388, called at Triplet.h:478-488. Order inside:
  a) Charge from 2D cross product of the 3 hits: charge = -sign((x2-x1)(y3-y1)-(y2-y1)(x3-x1)) (Triplet.h:172-173). No IP reference.
  b) Linear-interpolation regions (residual of z2 vs line through hits 1,3 in r-z, in meters), Triplet.h:161,176-194:
     - Region 9 (layer1=1, layer2=7): residual < 0.01 m
     - Region 20 (3,4,5): < 0.037127972 m
     - Region 21 (3,4,12): < 0.05 m
     - Region 22 (4,12,*): < 0.063831687 m
     - Region 23 (4,5,6): < 0.04362525 m
     - Region 24 (4,5,12): < 0.05 m
     (lstLayers numbering: barrel 1-6, endcap 7-11, 12-16 for 2S? — per ModuleMethods.h convention; regions map at the GitHub asset linked at Triplet.h:175.)
  c) All other regions: helix propagation. Momentum from circle fit: pt = 2*k2Rinv1GeVf*R (Triplet.h:232); px,py tangential at init point with quadrant sign fixes (Triplet.h:235-246); pz = dz/ds*pt with ds = R*dPhi, dPhi = acos(1 - AB2/(2R^2)) (Triplet.h:248-253). Init point = hit2 target = hit3, except regions 5 (8,14,15) and 19 (3,12,13) which use hit1->hit2 (Triplet.h:213-227). Residual: barrel target (layer3<=6 and (Center or drdz<1)) — closed-form z-solutions with 2 asin (Triplet.h:268-287); endcap target — helix x,y at s with sin/cos, residual in r (Triplet.h:288-296). Hit uncertainty: PS 0.15 cm, 2S 5.0 cm (Triplet.h:299); tilted-module projection factor cos/sin(atan(drdz)) computed algebraically (Triplet.h:301-306). rzChiSquared = 12*residual^2/(error^2*projection) (Triplet.h:308).
     NaN/negative-radius fallback: straight-line residual, rzChiSquared = 12*(residual/error)^2 < 2.8e-4 (Triplet.h:311-319).
     Per-region chi2 thresholds (Triplet.h:324-386): R0 (7,8,9)<65.47191; R1 (7,8,14)<3.3200853; R2 (7,13,*)<17.194584; R3 (8,9,10)<114.91959; R4 (8,9,15)<3.4359624; R5 (8,14,*)<4.6487956; R6 (9,10,11)<97.34339; R7 (9,10,16)<3.095819; R8 (9,15,*)<11.477617; R10 (1,*,7)<96.949936; R11 (1,*,3)<458.43982; R12 (2,7,8)<218.82303; R13 (2,7,13)<3.155554; R14 (2,3,7)<235.5005; R15 (2,3,12)<3.8522234; R16 (2,3,4)<3.5852437; R17 (3,7,8)<42.68; R18 (3,7,13)<3.853796; R19 (3,12,*)<6.2774787; any unlisted layer combination -> `return false` (Triplet.h:387).
  - IP assumption: INDIRECT. The helix uses only the 3 hits (no vertex constraint term), so the propagation itself is origin-free; but the per-region thresholds were tuned on prompt samples (PR SegmentLinking/cmssw#92 referenced at Triplet.h:160,323), and the fallback/linear regions were chosen on the same basis. No explicit z-window on the origin.

(S5) betaIn recompute + T3 DNN gate. runTripletConstraintsAndAlgo, Triplet.h:490-515:
  - betaIn recomputed exactly (with atan2 via cms::alpakatools::phi) for storage/DNN: betaIn = sdIn_alpha - reducePhiRange(phi(x3-x1,y3-y1) - anchorPhi(hit1)) (Triplet.h:502-505); betaInCut recomputed (Triplet.h:506-508) but only stored under CUT_VALUE_DEBUG — the actual betaIn cut was already applied in S2. IP assumption: YES (same anchorPhi/dPhiChange origin reference).
  - DNN: `lst::t3dnn::runInference(...)` (Triplet.h:510-513); returning false rejects the candidate ("T3-building cut", Triplet.h:512).

(S6) Occupancy cap (tryAddTriplet, Triplet.h:575-587): totOccupancyTriplets atomic vs ranges.tripletModuleOccupancy — see section 1. Cannot fire in ReduceMem mode (exact allocation) and is only a safety valve otherwise.

There are NO other cuts: no dz/dr window, no kDeltaZLum term, no explicit pT cut beyond betaInCut's ptCut dependence, at the T3 stage.

=====================================================================
3. THE T3 DNN
=====================================================================

Invocation: src/alpaka/Triplet.h:510-511 inside runTripletConstraintsAndAlgo (thus in CreateTriplets step 2 / ReduceMem step 1, and AGAIN in CountSegmentConnectionsReduceMem at Triplet.h:773-789). Implementation: src/alpaka/NeuralNetwork.h:65-141 (`namespace t3dnn::runInference`). Weights: src/alpaka/T3NeuralNetworkWeights.h (included via NeuralNetwork.h:11). Constants: interface/alpaka/Common.h:76-87.

Architecture: 14 -> 32 (Linear+ReLU) -> 32 (Linear+ReLU) -> 3 (Linear+Softmax) (NeuralNetwork.h:117-131).

Input features (NeuralNetwork.h:97-115), all from the 3 ANCHOR MDs (hit1 = inner LS first MD, hit2 = shared MD, hit3 = outer LS second MD); normalizations kEta_norm=2.5, kZ_max=224.149505 cm, kR_max=98.932365 cm, kPhi_norm=pi (Common.h:64,77-79):
 1. |eta1|/2.5              — ORIGIN-REFERENCING: anchorEta is pseudorapidity of the hit position vector from (0,0,0).
 2. |phi1|/pi               — origin-referencing (azimuth of position vector; |.| also assumes phi-symmetry).
 3. |z1|/kZ_max             — global z (beamspot-centered coordinate; z-symmetry assumed via abs).
 4. r1/kR_max               — transverse radius from beamline (origin-referencing).
 5. |eta2|-|eta1|           — difference; weakly origin-referencing (eta itself is origin-defined).
 6. deltaPhi(phi2,phi1)/pi  — difference of origin-defined phis; approximately origin-free for small opening.
 7. (|z2|-|z1|)/kZ_max      — difference.
 8. (r2-r1)/kR_max          — difference.
 9. |eta3|-|eta2|
10. deltaPhi(phi3,phi2)/pi
11. (|z3|-|z2|)/kZ_max
12. (r3-r2)/kR_max
13. log10(radius)           — circle-fit radius; origin-free (3-hit fit).
14. betaIn                  — ORIGIN-REFERENCING (built from dPhiChange and anchorPhi, both beamline-referenced; see S2/S5).
Summary of IP-flagged features: #1-#4 strongly (absolute position in origin-centered coords), #5,#6,#9,#10 mildly, #14 strongly.

Output classes (softmax over 3): output[0] = fake, output[1] = real prompt, output[2] = real displaced (Common.h/T3 comments; stored at Triplet.h:129-131).

Working-point cut at build time (NeuralNetwork.h:133-139): t3_pt = 2*k2Rinv1GeVf*radius; pt_index = (pt>5); eta bin = min(|eta1|/0.25, 9) (kEtaSize=0.25, kEtaBins=10, Common.h:65-67). PASS iff output[1] > kWp_prompt[pt][bin] OR output[2] > kWp_displaced[pt][bin]. Tables at Common.h:81-86 (e.g. low-pT prompt WPs 0.4957...0.5449; low-pT displaced WPs 0.0334...0.1847; high-pT prompt 0.0302...0.2187; high-pT displaced 0.0091...0.1046). Note: displaced OR-branch means T3s failing the prompt WP survive on displaced score alone.

Downstream consumers of the stored scores (fakeScore/promptScore/displacedScore, TripletsSoA.h:23-25):
- T5 embedding network t5embdnn::runEmbed — all 6 scores of the two T3s (+ score differences) are 6 of its 30 input features (NeuralNetwork.h:311-316,375-380); invoked inside runQuintupletDefaultAlgo at Quintuplet.h:1616-1632 (so also executed inside CountTripletConnectionsT dense/ReduceMem branch, Quintuplet.h:2082-2108). The embedding feeds T5 duplicate cleaning; no direct threshold on the raw T3 scores there.
- T4 DNN t4dnn::runInference — the 6 T3 scores + 3 differences are 9 of its 30 features (NeuralNetwork.h:458-463,519-527); called from runQuadrupletDefaultAlgo (Quadruplet.h:429-439); its own outputs are cut (displaced > WP && fake < WP, NeuralNetwork.h:557-558) and stored in QuadrupletsSoA.
- The T5 selection DNN (t5dnn::runInference, 23 features, NeuralNetwork.h:195-296) does NOT use T3 scores.
- pT3/pT5 kernels (PixelTriplet.h/PixelQuintuplet.h) do NOT read the T3 scores.
- Standalone ntuple writer reads them for t5_t3_*Score and t4_t3_*Score branches (standalone/code/core/write_lst_ntuple.cc:2835-2840,2896-2901).
- No later kernel cuts directly on stored T3 scores; the only *cut* is at build time inside t3dnn::runInference.

=====================================================================
4. TripletsSoA STORAGE (interface/TripletsSoA.h:12-46)
=====================================================================

Per-T3 columns (Params_T3: kLayers=3, kHits=6, interface/Common.h:71-76):
- preAllocatedSegmentIndices (uint x2, line 14): scratch used by two-phase CreateTriplets step 1 to stage candidate (innerSeg,outerSeg) pairs before RZ/DNN (Triplet.h:685-686, read back 701-702). Not meaningful after building.
- segmentIndices (uint x2, line 15): inner+outer LS indices of the accepted T3 (Triplet.h:96-97). Read by T5 building (Quintuplet.h:549-550,1511-1514,2039,2059-2065), T4 counting (Quadruplet.h:851,871-879), pT5 (PixelQuintuplet.h:516-519).
- lowerModuleIndices (uint16 x3, line 16): the 3 lower modules (Triplet.h:98-100). Drives T5/T4 outer-module chaining (Quintuplet.h:2054, Quadruplet.h:866) and pT3 storage.
- logicalLayers (uint8 x3, line 17): layer + 6 if endcap (Triplet.h:106-111); copied into pT3 (PixelTriplet.h:128-130).
- hitIndices (uint x6, line 18): anchor+outer hit of each MD (Triplet.h:117-122); copied into T4/T5/pT3 hit lists (Quadruplet.h:71-78, Quintuplet.h:77-81).
- betaIn (FPX half, line 19): stored chord angle (Triplet.h:102); ntuple/debug use.
- centerX, centerY, radius (float, lines 20-22): 3-anchor-hit exact circle fit from computeRadiusFromThreeAnchorHits (Circle.h:11-42; stored Triplet.h:103-105). radius is the pT proxy (pt = 2*k2Rinv1GeVf*R); read as innerRadius/outerRadius + (g,f) center seeds in T5 building (Quintuplet.h:1535-1537,1590) and pT3 radius matching (PixelTriplet.h:629).
- fakeScore, promptScore, displacedScore (float, lines 23-25): the T3 DNN softmax outputs (Triplet.h:129-131); consumers per section 3.
- connectedMax (uint, line 26): number of outer T3s that (a) share the T3's last MD (secondMDOuter==thirdMDInner) and (b) in the dense (>= kNTripletThreshold = 1000, Common.h:46) or ReduceMem case also pass the full runQuintupletDefaultAlgo — filled by CountTripletConnectionsT (Quintuplet.h:2026-2118, atomics at 2070,2110); summed by CreateEligibleModulesListForQuintuplets to size the T5 allocation per module (Quintuplet.h:2149-2164).
- connectedLSMax (uint, line 27): same idea for T4s but with the stricter LS-equality condition (secondMDInner==thirdMDInner && secondMDOuter==thirdMDOuter, i.e. shared middle SEGMENT) — filled by CountTripletLSConnectionsT (Quadruplet.h:838-925, atomics at 884,916); summed for T4 allocation (Quadruplet.h:956-971).
- charge (short, line 28): from the xy cross-product orientation (Triplet.h:172-173, stored 124); read by T4 building for charge matching (Quadruplet.h:327-328).
- betaInCut (float, CUT_VALUE_DEBUG only, lines 29-31; Triplet.h:125-127).
- partOfPT5 / partOfT5 / partOfPT3 (bool, lines 32-34): usage flags set by PixelQuintuplet.h:732-733, Quintuplet.h:2005-2006, PixelTriplet.h:827; read for pT3 cross-cleaning (PixelTriplet.h:767) and T4 cross-cleaning (Quadruplet.h:582-596).
Occupancy SoA (lines 40-42): nTriplets, totOccupancyTriplets per lower module.

=====================================================================
5. PER-CANDIDATE COST PROFILE
=====================================================================

Amortized per inner segment (loadT3InnerSegData, Triplet.h:45-77): ~12 SoA loads (2 mdIndices, 4 anchorX/Y, 2 anchorRt, dPhiChanges, dPhiChangeMins, dPhiChangeMaxs, 2 subdets), 1 sqrt, 2 sin/cos (6 if EEE). Divided by nOuterSegments of the middle module.

Common reject path A — MD mismatch (vast majority of pairs), Triplet.h:643-647: 1 SoA read (mdIndices[outerSeg][0]; mdIndices[inner][1] hoisted at 636). 0 transcendentals, 0 FLOPs beyond compare. This is the whole cost for most candidates.

Reject path B — fails pointing constraint (Triplet.h:649-655 + passPointingConstraint 390-437): +4 SoA reads (outerLowerModuleIndices, mdIndices[outer][1], anchorX[third], anchorY[third], subdets[outerOuter] = 5 total) ; transcendentals: 1 sqrt (drt_tl_axis), 1 asin (betaInCut), 1 sin (sinBetaInCut) = 3 (EEE path identical count; per-alpha sin/cos are hoisted). ~40 FLOPs of arithmetic. No DNN, no RZ.

Reject path C — passes pointing, fails RZ (tryAddTriplet -> runTripletConstraintsAndAlgo, Triplet.h:457-488):
- Extra SoA reads: 3 mdIndices + 12 anchor coords (x,y,z,rt for 3 MDs) = 15; in the non-ReduceMem two-phase path add 2 preAllocatedSegmentIndices writes + 2 reads + 2 outerLowerModuleIndices reads (Triplet.h:685-705). passRZConstraint module reads: lstLayers x3, moduleType, drdzs, sides, subdets = 7 (Triplet.h:146-148,197,263-265).
- Transcendentals: circle fit 1 sqrt (Circle.h:39). RZ linear regions (9,20-24): 0 extra. RZ helix: 1 acos (Triplet.h:251), 1 sqrt p (255); barrel target: 1 sqrt disc + 2 asin (277-281); endcap target: 1 sin + 1 cos + 1 sqrt (291-295). Worst-case RZ ~5 transcendentals; typical 4.
- ~120-150 FLOPs of plain arithmetic.

Reject path D — passes RZ, fails DNN: adds betaIn recompute — 2 sqrt (Triplet.h:493-500), 1 atan2 (cms::alpakatools::phi -> atan2, deltaPhi.h:19-20), 1 asin (betaInCut, Triplet.h:507), 1 anchorPhi read — then the full DNN:
- DNN inputs: 15 SoA reads (anchorEta/Phi/Z/Rt x3 = 12 + already-loaded coords not reused: eta/phi are NEW columns; z/r re-read via mds despite hitCoords — actually 12 reads at NeuralNetwork.h:80-94).
- DNN transcendentals: 1 log10 (NeuralNetwork.h:113) + 3 exp in softmax (NeuralNetwork.h:25). deltaPhi(phi_i,phi_j) is subtraction + range reduction, no atan2 (HeterogeneousCore/AlpakaMath/deltaPhi.h:29-31).
- DNN FLOPs: linear layers 14x32 + 32x32 + 32x3 = 448+1024+96 = 1568 MACs ~= 3136 FLOPs, + 32+32+3 bias adds included, + 64 ReLU compares, + softmax (3 exp, 3 div, 2 add). Weight-table reads: 1568 floats + 67 biases from constant memory (~6.5 KB, cached).

Accept path (all of the above plus addTripletToMemory, Triplet.h:79-132): 2 atomicAdds (totOccupancy, nTriplets; Triplet.h:576-589) + 1 ranges read; writes: 2 segIdx + 3 lowerModules + 3 logicalLayers (with 3 layers + 3 subdets module reads) + 6 hitIndices (with 2 mdIndices + 6 hit-index reads) + betaIn + radius + centerX/Y + charge + 3 scores ~= 22 column writes, ~14 extra reads.
Total accept-path transcendentals: 3 (pointing) + 1 (circle sqrt) + ~4 (RZ) + 4 (betaIn recompute: 2 sqrt, atan2, asin) + 1 log10 + 3 exp ~= 16, dominated in FLOP terms by the ~3.1 kFLOP DNN.

ReduceMem double-cost caveat: with reduceMemByFullPrecompute_ the ENTIRE accept-path cost (RZ + DNN) is paid twice per surviving candidate — once in CountSegmentConnectionsReduceMem (Triplet.h:769-790) and once in CreateTripletsReduceMem — in exchange for exact allocation. In the default mode the precount pays only paths A/B (MD + pointing, Triplet.h:756-765), and RZ+DNN are paid once, but the Triplets buffer is sized to the pointing-constraint-passing superset (typically larger than the final T3 count) and additionally carries the preAllocatedSegmentIndices staging column for every allocated row.

## 1. Construction, combinatorics, occupancy machinery

**Definition**: A T4 = 2 T3s sharing their middle **LS** (not just a middle MD as in T5). The inner T3's second segment must be *identical* (same LS index) to the outer T3's first segment: `src/alpaka/Quadruplet.h:599-604` (`innerT3LS2Index != outerT3LS1Index → continue`). So a T4 spans 4 MDs / 8 hits / 4 layers (`Params_T4::kLayers = 4, kHits = 8`, `interface/Common.h:83-88`). MD indices: MD1 = inner T3 seg1 MD0, MD2 = inner T3 seg2 MD0, MD3 = inner T3 seg2 MD1, MD4 = outer T3 seg2 MD1 (`Quadruplet.h:332-335`).

**Region restriction**: `isValidQuadRegion` (`Quadruplet.h:830-835`): T4s are only seeded from modules with `(subdet==Barrel && layer > 2) || subdet==Endcap` — comment at :833 "Quadruplets starting outside these regions are not built." Additionally in the build kernel, barrel layer-1/2 starting modules are skipped (must be Endcap if layer==1 or 2, `Quadruplet.h:558-570`). So barrel T4s occupy outer layers (L3-L6); endcap T4s any ring — i.e., the phase space where a 5-layer T5 is impossible or the track enters late (displaced/large-eta).

**Combinatoric loop** (`CreateQuadrupletsT`, `Quadruplet.h:516-825`): 3D kernel, grid-z over eligible modules (workdiv `{nEligibleT4Modules,1,1} x {1,8,32}`, `LSTEvent.dev.cc:1253-1254`). LS sharing here is tested by MD-pair equality (`secondMDInner==thirdMDInner && secondMDOuter==thirdMDOuter`, :881) — no partOf veto, so it is an upper bound.

## 5. GPU vs CPU backend differences relevant to a redesign

- Single portable source: no `#ifdef ALPAKA_ACC_GPU_CUDA_ENABLED` branches in any kernel of this branch (grep hits only fp16 includes in Common.h:7-13 and blockDim queries); no `requires_single_thread_per_block_v` specializations here (those live in the user's separate cpu_speedups branches). Backend divergence is entirely via Alpaka semantics:
  - On CPU serial, `cms::alpakatools::make_workdiv<AccND>(blocks, threads)` converts "threads per block" into per-thread ELEMENTS (1 OS thread per block); `uniform_elements_x/y/z` become sequential loops. So the Acc3D {module,1,1},{1,8,32} kernels degenerate to: outer loop over modules (blocks, one per module), inner sequential 8x32=256-element loops. Grid-level parallelism on CPU comes only from blocks; the {1},{1024} single-block prefix-sum kernels are fully serial on CPU.
  - Atomics: all occupancy counters use `alpaka::atomicAdd(..., alpaka::hierarchy::Threads{})` (e.g. MiniDoublet.h:780, Segment.h:998, Triplet.h:668, Quintuplet.h:2070). `hierarchy::Threads` requires the counting kernels to have exactly 1 block in x,y (asserted, Segment.h:933-934, Triplet.h:730-731, Quintuplet.h:2036-2037); on serial CPU these compile to plain increments (free), on GPU they are block-scope atomics (cheaper than device scope). ExtendT5FromDupT5 additionally uses `alpaka::atomicCas` retry loops on shared uint64 (Kernels.h:477-478).
  - Shared memory: used sparingly - single int accumulators (`matchCount`, `nTotal*`) in build/range kernels (Triplet.h:534, Quintuplet.h:1711, Quadruplet.h:532, Segment.h:1017, MiniDoublet.h:893) and ExtendT5FromDupT5's ~452 bytes (11 x uint64 + 40 x (2 x uint32 + uint8) + uint32, Kernels.h:295-299). Nothing approaches the 48 KB/block CUDA budget; shared memory is used for block coordination, not data staging. On CPU, declareSharedVar is just a stack variable per block.
  - Block-two-phase pattern (collect pairs -> syncBlockThreads -> process) in CreateTriplets/CreateQuintuplets/CreateQuadruplets exists to load-balance GPU threads; on CPU it is pure overhead (the phase-1/phase-2 split serializes anyway). The dense-module serial fallback (Quintuplet.h:1767-1768, Quadruplet.h:606) exists to avoid `preAllocatedSegmentIndices` truncation for >=1000-triplet modules.
  - Block sizes used on GPU: 256 (hits), 512 (16x32 MD), 256 (1x8x32 LS/T5/T4 build/count), 256 (1x16x16 T3), 1024 (range kernels, also max CUDA block size), 128 (ExtendT5, 1D), 1024 (32x1x32 crosscleans), 1024 (8x128 T5/T4 adders), 128 (4x1x32 pT3 build), 256 (16x1x16 pT5 build), 256 (16x16 dup removals). `max_blocks=80` tuned for GPU SM count; on CPU stream-level parallelism (up to 64 streams in timing runs) provides the throughput instead.
  - Host round-trips (section 1) are synchronization bottlenecks on GPU (each `alpaka::wait` drains the stream, ~10 per event) but nearly free on CPU serial where the queue is synchronous. A redesign eliminating host-side allocation decisions (e.g. device-side allocation or graph capture) benefits GPU only. The triplet-stage nonZeroModules compaction is done on host with a device->host->device bounce (LSTEvent.dev.cc:462-498) and is flagged "FIXME: replace by ES host data" (line 468).
  - Half precision: `FPX = __half` only when FP16_Base defined on GPU backends (Common.h:46-54); on CPU FPX = float. Kernels convert via `__H2F` (e.g. Kernels.h:321-322), so numerics can differ CPU vs GPU when FP16 is enabled.
  - Serial-backend ES sharing: modules/endcapGeometry shared_ptr shared across streams on host without copy (LSTESData.h:21-24, 58-60).

5. EXISTING MITIGATIONS AND CLAIMED EFFECT
=====================================================================

a) Dense-path serialization, kNTripletThreshold=1000 (interface/alpaka/Common.h:46; Quintuplet.h:1768, 2069; Quadruplet.h:607, 883): purpose is correctness (comment Quintuplet.h:1767 "If densely connected, do not attempt parallel processing to avoid truncation"), not speed — it PREVENTS pair-slot preallocation overflow by evaluating inline, at the cost of running the full heavy algo per pair inside one block, twice (count + create). b) Shared-middle-MD scan test (Quintuplet.h:1764): claimed selectivity in-code = only "factor of 3" at warp level (comment line 1763).

   - Two-phase refactor (9810ef47bb3): compatible-module selection threaded over modules first, then candidate scan threaded over T5s (Kernels.h:346-383 vs 386-487) — removes per-T5 redundant module filtering.

The only in-cone discriminators are hit-index compares and the embed distance.

=====================================================================
6. QUANTITATIVE MODEL: k tracks x 5 layers in a cone hitting m hot modules/layer
=====================================================================

Assumptions: collimated core (DR < 0.05) so all eta/phi windows pass; per hot module per layer: nMD ~ k (plus merged-cluster fakes; call it h ~ 1-2k); module connection fanout <= 40 (max_connected_modules, interface/Common.h:28) but in-cone only the m ~ 1-3 next-layer modules matter.

Per hot module chain (layer i -> i+1 -> i+2 ...):
- LS: pairs visited h^2 per connected module pair; jet-core pass fraction f_LS is HIGH (all tracks nearly parallel, dPhi/dz windows tuned for 0.8 GeV generic tracks): nLS ~ f_LS h^2, f_LS ~ 0.2-1. (k=25, f_LS=0.5 -> nLS ~ 300/module.)
- T3: pairs visited nLS x nLS ~ f_LS^2 h^4 (Triplet.h:631-647), each pair costing ~3 ops; MD-matched pairs ~ f_LS^2 h^4/h = f_LS^2 h^3 each paying pointing (~25 flops); survivors x f_point pay RZ + fit + DNN (~1800 flops). nT3(module) ~ f_T3 f_LS^2 h^3 with f_T3 ~ 0.05-0.3. For h=25-50: nT3 ~ 10^2-10^4 -> this is exactly how modules cross the kNTripletThreshold=1000 dense trigger. ALL of the above x2 (count kernel Triplet.h:736 + create kernel).
- T5: pairs visited nT3(m1) x nT3(m3) ~ (f_T3 f_LS^2 h^3)^2 = O(h^6) per module pair — SIXTH power of core hit multiplicity (Quintuplet.h:1748-1765). MD-matched ~ h^6 x f/h = O(h^5), each paying the ~40-load/~1900-MAC DNN prefix (section 2), x2 kernels. Numeric: nT3=10^3 both sides -> 10^6 visits, ~4x10^4 MD-matched, ~8x10^4 full-prefix evaluations ~ 1.6x10^8 flops for ONE module pair, executed inside ONE 256-thread block in the dense path (both in CountTripletConnections {1,8,32} and CreateQuintuplets {1,8,32}) -> ~6x10^5 serial flops/thread; this block is the event's critical path.
- Surviving T5s: N_T5(jet) ~ f_T5 x h^5-ish; empirically the same 5 hits generate T5s in C(dup combinations) — a single real track with 2 hits/layer ambiguities can yield 2^5=32 T5 variants; k tracks with cross-track confusion give N_T5(jet) ~ 10^2-10^4.
- T4: visited nT3(m1) x nT3(m2) ~ h^6 again, but LS-equality pass ~ h^6/nLS = h^4, and partOf flags remove T5-claimed T3s.
- Dedup: RemoveDupQuintupletsAfterBuild ~ sum_mod n_T5(mod)^2/2; RemoveDupQuintupletsBeforeTC ~ N_T5(jet)^2/2 pairs visited (no in-cone prefilter power), each ~200 int cmp + 6 MACs, with n1 x n2 chunks serialized on single threads (Kernels.h:530-540); for N_T5(jet)=3x10^3: ~5x10^6 pair visits ~ 10^9 int ops event-critical-path. ExtendT5FromDupT5 ~ N_T5(jet)^2 candidate visits but with the 8-hit 1-2-cmp prefilter constant (Kernels.h:394-413), so ~10^7 cheap ops for the same N.
- pT3: n_pLS(cone) x n_T3(hot) ~ (2k) x 10^3 = 5x10^4 radius-tests per jet (cheap constant), survivors paying window+chi2+DNN; output pressed against the GLOBAL 5000 cap (Common.h:34).
- pT5: n_pLS(cone) x n_T5(hot) ~ (2k) x 10^3 with a ~21-load un-hoisted constant per pair (PixelQuintuplet.h:493).
- Pixel dedup: nPT3^2 (up to 25M pairs at cap, no prefilter, Kernels.h:723-751).

Summary ranking of jet-core cost drivers (visits x per-visit constant, per jet):
1. T5 dense path: O(h^6) visits with 3-op constant + O(h^5) MD-matched with ~2000-flop constant, x2 kernels, serialized to one block/module — dominant.
2. RemoveDupQuintupletsBeforeTC: O(N_T5^2) with ~200-op constant, single-thread-serial per module pair, no effective in-cone prefilter.
3. T3 build: O(h^4) visits x2 kernels (small constant), plus O(h^3) x ~1600-MAC DNN.
4. ExtendT5FromDupT5: O(N_T5^2) but ~1-op prefilter constant after lst019 (was ~100-op full hit match).
5. pT3/pT5 maps: O(k x nT3/nT5(hot)) products, plus event-global caps 5000/15000 as the silent efficiency cliff.
